summary.text: One of the twenty-three suitors from Same on Cephallenia in Apollodorus' catalogue — a namesake of Hyperenor the Spartan, Hyperenor son of Panthous at Troy, and Hyperenor among the Theban Spartoi.

story.text: Apollodorus counts Hyperenor among the wooers who came from Same, named after Pisenor and before Pheroetes in the island list of Penelope's suitors.

Homer's Iliad knows a Trojan Hyperenor, son of Panthous and tamer of horses, slain by Menelaus; Apollodorus elsewhere names Hyperenor among the five Spartoi and among sons of Pleione — none of whom is this Same suitor.
